Honoré de Balzac, Father Goriot, translated by Ellen Marriage.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/honore-de-balzac/father-goriot/ellen-marriage

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- Honoré de Balzac, the author, died 1850 or 1851 (Wikidata Q9711, P570 1850-08-18 and 1851-08-19).
- Ellen Marriage, the translator and annotator, died 1946 (Wikidata Q5364934, P570 1946-12-23).

First publication of the text used: 1896, the English translation by Ellen Marriage. The French original was published between 1834 and 1835. The country of first publication of the translation is not stated in the facts. (SE colophon: 'Father Goriot was published between 1834 and 1835 by Honoré de Balzac. It was translated from French in 1896 by Ellen Marriage.')

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the translation was first published in 1896 and the original in 1834 and 1835, both before 1931, so the text is in the United States public domain. The edition's rights statement quoted below says the same.
- Country of origin: Two layers, checked separately. Original: French work by Honoré de Balzac (died 1850 or 1851), first published between 1834 and 1835. The author died before 1926, so the original is public domain in every country. Translation (English): the possible countries are the United Kingdom, Ireland, the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, India and South Africa. Each has a term of life + 70 years or less. The translator Ellen Marriage (died 1946) left the public domain in each of them on 1 January 2017, so the translation is public domain in each. The country of first publication therefore makes no difference.

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."

Sources of these facts:
- SE colophon of this edition (https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/honore-de-balzac/father-goriot/ellen-marriage): quoted above.
- Wikidata Q9711 (Honoré de Balzac), P570 1850-08-18 and 1851-08-19.
